registry_info.name: taxonomy_hall
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `taxonomy` family (7 registry names, 6 scripts, 2 declaration orders). One set of eight specimens standing in four bays at once, so the four claims can be compared instead of chosen between.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The `taxonomy` word and its four values are PRELOADED from combine_sphere.gd at runtime and checked in both directions at _ready; do not retype them here or in the script. The two axes declared below are NOT that word — see dna.declines.

taxonomy_hall.name: Taxonomy Hall
taxonomy_hall.description: Eight specimens, made once, standing four times over. Four bays on one apron hold the same eight prisms as a table (a 4x2 lattice in accession order), a ladder (one ascending file), a stack (one column, each body resting on the one below) and a heap (a hashed pile with the smallest lifted to the mouth) — the family's four words, read out of combine_sphere's own const at build time and never retyped. `key` changes the character the ordering is taken on: bulk, a magnitude; made, a provenance that is not a property at all; sides, a count with ties; hue, a circle with no smallest value. `gauge` changes how much of the access discipline is drawn: nothing; a rail of eight bars per bay, one per member, in the order that bay yields them and as tall as that member's rank; plus a collar on everything the claim gives you in one step; plus a column for what the whole claim charges. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one rank array per key at build time, read three ways.
interactions: walk the four bays and find the one that never moves when the key changes
read the four rank rails against each other: the ladder ascends, the stack is its mirror, the heap is the ladder again, the table is scrambled
set key=made and watch three of the four rails become the same staircase
set key=sides and find the three tied pairs, and see which way the tie was broken
at toll, notice that the two columns are the same height and ask whether a stack and a heap are therefore the same thing
taxonomy_hall.qfep_connection: Four ways to arrange one set, standing at once so that none of them can pass as the natural one. The hall cannot exempt itself: putting four claims side by side on a common apron is itself the table claim, the most innocent-looking of the four, and the artifact says so rather than pretending to a view from nowhere. What the gauge then shows is that the ranking never lived in the objects — change the character from bulk to hue and the ladder, the stack and the heap all rearrange completely while the table does not move a millimetre, because a table is the one claim that never asserted an order to be wrong about.
taxonomy_hall.relationships: synthesis over the `taxonomy` family; adopts its word by exhibiting it rather than sweeping it; closest relative is math_objects_gallery, which varies the same word over 33 parametric surfaces

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 3.04 m across the four bays by 0.53 m deep, so a 4 x 1 clear strip with room to stand in front of it. The gauge rail is on the +Z edge and every bay reads from that side, so the artifact wants approaching from +Z; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. There is no collider anywhere in the file — the pathfinder will route straight through the stack, which is correct, because there is no stack, there is a picture of one.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh or a SurfaceTool prism. There is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG, no particle system and no Label3D, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present. X = 4 bays at 0.760 pitch, plus a 0.340 bay half-width and 0.040 of apron margin each side: 3 x 0.760 + 2 x 0.380 = 3.04. Y runs from 0 (the apron underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 1.165 = the plinth top at 0.210 plus the sum of all eight specimen heights, 0.955, which is the `stack` bay and is the tallest thing in the hall at every value of both axes. Z from -0.300 (apron back) to +0.230 (apron front lip, 0.045 clear of the gauge rail at 0.160). The box is IDENTICAL at every value of `key` and grows only in Y-independent ways at `toll`, whose columns top out at 0.470 and are therefore never the tallest thing; so the camera does not move between tiles for any reason other than the sweep's own union pre-pass.

dna.axis_shape: `key` sits SIDE BY SIDE — four different KINDS of character (a magnitude, a provenance, a count with ties, a circle with no origin), none of which contains another, so they are a set and any two of them are a comparison. `gauge` NESTS — none is contained in rank is contained in mouth is contained in toll, each rung keeping every mark the last one drew, so it is a sequence and must be swept in order. Both are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming: dropping the tail of a parallel axis loses a case, dropping the tail of a nested one only lowers the ceiling.
dna.default:
key=bulk, gauge=mouth. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `bulk` AND NOT `made`. `made` is the loudest key — at accession order the rank rails of the table, the ladder and the heap all become the SAME ascending staircase, which is a striking frame and the wrong default, because it is the one key where the machinery is broken: accession is not a property of the objects at all, so what the frame shows is three claims agreeing about nothing. `bulk` is the only key where a total order is honest — no ties, nothing arbitrary, every member strictly greater than the last, with the two closest volumes 0.80% apart (0.001107386 against 0.001116300 cubic metres) — so every difference visible between the four bays is a difference between the CLAIMS rather than an artefact of a broken character. A visitor who meets only the default meets the question. `made`, `sides` and `hue` are the three ways the character itself fails, and they are one token away.

WHY `mouth` AND NOT `toll`. `toll` is the fullest rung and the most misleading single frame: its two columns are the same height to the millimetre, which says a stack and a heap are the same object. They are not — one yields its members largest first and the other smallest first, which the rank rail shows and which the scoreboard erases. `mouth` carries the rail AND the access marks and asserts nothing it cannot show. `none` is the emptiest rung by definition: four arrangements and no way to say what any of them claims, which is a picture of the question rather than of the artifact.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the seven `taxonomy` declarations leave unbuilt: every member's own note describes the four values as four CLAIMS about one set, and not one of them can stand two of those claims at the same time, because a body can only be arranged one way at once.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A HALL RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

The family's four words are four different claims about one set. A table says the members are commensurable: same columns, no order, every cell independently addressable. A ladder says they are ranked. A stack says only the top is reachable. A heap says there is no order at all, just a pile with a smallest element. Seven registry names declare this word and every one of them STANDS IN one claim and forgoes the other three; none of them can put a table next to the heap of the same objects, so none of them can show that the four are incompatible rather than merely different-looking.

So the hall builds the set ONCE — eight prisms, each differing from every other in side count, radius, height and hue — and stands it four times on one apron, in the family's own order, read live from combine_sphere.gd. What varies instead is the SECOND decision every taxonomy makes and the family never varies: what the arrangement is an arrangement BY.

WHAT IT FOUND, all of it computed in Python before anything was built.

(1) THE TABLE DOES NOT MOVE. Across all four keys, at gauge=none, the table bay is pixel-identical — verified in the replica: the leftmost changed column between any two key values is 278-282, and the table bay's plinth ends at column 236. It does not move because it is the only claim that does not assert an order, so it has no key to change; it lays its eight out in accession order and says nothing about the sequence. Three quarters of the hall rearranges and one quarter is untouched, in every key pair, by construction. THIS IS THE FINDING, NOT A DEAD BAY, and it is why the still_note says so in advance.

(2) THE HEAP YIELDS EXACTLY THE LADDER'S ORDER, at every key, always. Both hand their members over ascending by rank; the rank rails of those two bays are therefore the same staircase in every one of the sixteen tiles. A heap is a ladder that has not been written down yet — the order is all there, it just costs you something to read it. The stack's rail is that same staircase reversed.

(3) STACK AND HEAP CHARGE THE SAME TOLL, 28, AND ARE MIRRORS IN WHO PAYS. cost[i] is the number of OTHER members you must handle before member i is in your hand: for the stack it is 8 - rank (the bodies above it), for the heap it is rank - 1 (the bodies smaller than it). Both sum to 8*7/2 = 28 for any key. So the `toll` rung draws two columns of identical height beside two obviously different objects — which is the point of drawing it. A scoreboard that cannot tell a stack from a heap is a fact about scoreboards.

(4) TABLE AND LADDER CHARGE NOTHING, AND THAT IS STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN INVENTED AWAY. A ranked file leaves every rung exposed; ranking is a claim about order, not a gate. So table and ladder measure ALIKE at `mouth` (eight collars each) and at `toll` (no column each), and the only thing that separates them anywhere in this artifact is the rank rail, where the ladder's ascends and the table's is scrambled. Giving the ladder a fictitious sequential-access toll would have made a livelier picture and a false one.

(5) THE FOUR KEYS FAIL IN THREE DIFFERENT WAYS, and that is the axis rather than a flaw in it. `bulk` is a clean total order. `sides` has three tied pairs (3, 4 and 6 are each shared by two specimens), so six of eight members are tied with another and the ladder's rungs 1-2, 3-4 and 6-7 are in accession order — the arbitrary tiebreak made visible. `hue` is circular: the ordering exists only because the file cuts the circle at 0 degrees, and a cut at 180 would give a different first rung and a different heap apex. `made` is not a property of the objects at all. Only one of the four characters can carry the weight the ladder, the stack and the heap all put on it.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NOT RETYPED. taxonomy_hall.gd opens with
const TAX_SRC := preload("res://commons/primitives/combines/combine_sphere.gd")
and the bays, their number and their order come from TAX_SRC's own TAXONOMIES at build time, read through get_script_constant_map() rather than Object.get() — a const is not a property, so get() would have returned null and the hall would have fallen back silently to its own copy, which is the exact drift the preload exists to prevent. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a value the family declares that this hall has no bay for, and a bay this hall builds that the family has dropped. combine_sphere is the one read because combine_capsule.gd and math_objects_gallery.gd both name it in their own comments as where they took the word from.

THE ORDER THIS HALL TOOK, AND THE ONE IT DID NOT. Six of the seven members declare table | ladder | stack | heap, character for character, and they do so regardless of their own default — combine_portals defaults to "ladder" and still lists table first, so this family does NOT hoist a default the way the `slack` family does. grammar_totem_pole_rainbow_taper declares stack | ladder | table | heap, which is the six-member order with table and stack swapped (not a hoist of its "stack" default either, which would have given stack | table | ladder | heap). This hall takes the six-member order, because that is the const it preloads and that is what six of seven agree on.

WHAT THE TWO ORDERS ACTUALLY COST, which is narrower than it looks. build_dna_gallery trims a value list from the TAIL, so two orders could mean two different values dropped first. Here they mostly do not: BOTH orders end in `heap`, so at a cap leaving 3 values the family is measured on the SAME SET {table, ladder, stack} and only the tile order differs. Divergence appears only at cap 2, where the totem would be measured on {stack, ladder} while the other six are measured on {table, ladder} — one value in common out of two. The hazard is real and it has a threshold: a single-axis `taxonomy` sweep at --max 3 or above compares like with like.

THE ORDER OF THIS HALL'S OWN TWO AXES. Default first, then the code's declaration order minus the default, which is slack_yard's convention:
  key    code order bulk, made, sides, hue; default bulk, already first -> unchanged
  gauge  code order none, rank, mouth, toll (the nested ladder, bottom up); default
         mouth -> mouth | none | rank | toll
At the gallery's DEFAULT cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2: `key` keeps all four values and `gauge` is trimmed to [mouth, none], which is the default against the empty rung — a large number (predicted 27.74-28.15% focus) that would be a verdict about two rungs published as a verdict about four. THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=16.

WHY THE HALL DOES NOT REUSE ANOTHER FAMILY'S WORD FOR ITS OWN AXES. `key` and `gauge` are both new to this corpus (0 prior declarations each, checked across all 968 declared axes). `chapter` (facade_grammar_demo: all|topology|organic|compound|decoration|bridge) was considered for `key` and refused: that axis asks which SUBSET of a collection is on the table, and every value but `all` removes members. Nothing is ever removed here. `datum` (slack_yard: gauged|none|beside|scored) was considered for `gauge` and refused for the opposite reason: it is a good word for it, but it belongs to the `slack` family's argument about a measured deviation from a true curve, and there is no true arrangement here for the hall to deviate from — borrowing the word would claim a comparability that does not exist.
dna.declines:
`taxonomy` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design.

The four values sit SIDE BY SIDE, and this was read out of the members' CODE rather than their prose. In combine_capsule.gd, combine_sphere.gd, math_objects_gallery.gd and facade_grammar_demo.gd the word is spent in a single `match taxonomy:` inside one placement function returning ONE position per member: "ladder", "stack" and "heap" each DISCARD the lattice cell and re-site the member from its index alone, and `_:` returns the untouched lattice. Four mutually exclusive returns from one switch — no value contains another, and there is no all-at-once reading that is secretly the top rung. grammar_totem_pole_rainbow_taper is the same switch over eight authored parts.

Parallel values means the simultaneity is the object: hold all four standing and vary something else. An axis on the word would demolish three quarters of the exhibit at every turn, and the big number it produced would be a measurement of the hall being dismantled.

THE RECURSION WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, and it is the interesting decline. Four bays exhibiting four claims is itself a set of four, and the hall could have applied the family word to its own bays — a row of bays (table), a rising file of bays (ladder), a column of bays (stack), a pile of bays (heap) — which demolishes nothing, since all four wings stand in every value. It is the sharpest thing this artifact could say, and it was refused for a mechanical reason: the registry would then carry an eighth `taxonomy` declaration with the same four values as the other seven, and every tool that groups a family by axis name would compare its bite against theirs as though it measured the same thing. It does not: theirs re-site MEMBERS, this one would re-site BAYS. Two tools disagreeing about the same tokens is the tell this corpus keeps rediscovering, and the fix is not to create the ambiguity.

So the recursion is stated in prose instead of swept: the hall's four bays stand in a row on a common apron, each on an identical plinth, in the family's own order — which IS the table claim, the most innocent-looking of the four. The hall cannot stand outside the question it asks, and it does not pretend to.

PER-MEMBER CAPTIONS ARE ALSO DECLINED, and this is a departure from the family. Every member's note calls the captions the pivot and `heap` the value that withholds them. This hall carries no text at all: at 209.09 px per metre a legible glyph would have to be about 8 cm tall, two thirds the height of the smallest specimen, and the tallest specimen is 23 cm. Identity is carried by the BODY instead — no two of the eight share a side count, a radius, a height or a hue, so each specimen is its own name. That is honest here and would not be on the combine benches, where the members are near-identical capsules and the numbers exist only on the plates.
dna.measured: SWEPT 2026-08-12 at --max=16, all sixteen frames, and THE PREDICTION WAS RIGHT ABOUT BOTH THE PAIR AND THE CLUSTERING. It named gauge `rank` against `mouth` at all four keys and said they should cluster; measured, they are 0.88% (hue), 0.95% (made), 0.95% (sides), 0.97% (bulk) — a spread of nine hundredths of a point across four contexts. `key` is the healthy axis at 1.50-2.91%, weakest at hue against made in every gauge. `gauge` runs 0.88-4.45%, with mouth-against-rank the floor everywhere and mouth-against-none or toll-against-none the ceiling. Note what the 10.4% subject share does NOT mean here: the framing is not at fault. The union box spans 75.7% of frame width by construction, but four separated bays standing on an apron leave most of that box empty, so a pixel count against the background reads low for a correctly framed object. A sparse subject is not a small one. Left alone: rank draws bars and mouth draws collars, they are different marks for different claims, and the two readings are close because the claims are close.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5% (1,280 samples). Every number below comes from rasterising this exact geometry at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.58) in Python with a z-buffer and pushing the result through that same pipeline.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS gauge `rank` <-> `mouth`, AT ALL FOUR KEYS, AND THEY SHOULD CLUSTER. Predicted focus 9.74% (hue), 9.86% (sides), 10.01% (bulk), 10.33% (made) — a spread of 0.59 points across the whole axis. That tightness is half the claim: the rung adds EXACTLY 18 collars in every key (table 8, ladder 8, stack 1, heap 1) and the only thing the key changes is which members wear them, so the only source of variation is the radius of the collared bodies. If the sweep returns a spread of more than about two points on this pair, something is reading the key that should not be.

THE ARITHMETIC. At key=bulk the two frames differ over 3,533 px of a 187,450 px crop (1.885%) with a mean absolute difference of 122.9 grey levels over the changed pixels — near-white cyan collars against a mid-grey plinth top. Total change energy 3,533 x 122.9 = 434,200 grey-levels; scaled into the 25,600-sample crop that is 59,300; and the hottest 1,280 samples carry 1,280 x 0.1001 x 255 = 32,700 of it, i.e. 55%, the rest being lost to the 4.7x downsample smearing a 26-55 px collar across partial samples. That accounting is the prediction; if the measured focus comes back near 18% the resize is not smearing the way the replica says it is, and if it comes back near 2% the collars did not render.

A SECOND PREDICTION, STRONGER BECAUSE IT IS AN EQUALITY. The six `key` pairs measured at gauge=mouth and the six measured at gauge=toll must be THE SAME NUMBERS, to about four decimal places. In the replica they agree to within 4.9e-05 (e.g. made|bulk 0.231903 against 0.231887, made|hue identical to the byte at 0.204611). The reason is structural: `toll` adds two columns whose height is the sum of a bay's costs, and that sum is 28 for the stack and 28 for the heap at EVERY key, so the toll marks are the same pixels in all four key tiles and cancel out of a key difference. The residual comes only from the subject bounding box growing slightly when the columns are present. If those twelve numbers do not pair up, the toll is reading the key, and it must not.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be. `mouth` and `toll` differ by two columns and nothing else — the obvious twin candidate on a 16-tile sheet, and the pair most likely to be dismissed as a rounding of the same frame. Predicted 15.89% (made), 15.94% (bulk and hue), 15.95% (sides): NOT a twin, well clear of the critic's 6% bar. The columns are 0.110 x 0.440 m of near-white against the void and the plinth face — 23.0 x 92.0 px each, 5,876 changed pixels for the pair, 1.66x the collar rung's 3,533. It is the sparsest mark in the artifact and it is not thin.

AXIS MEANS PREDICTED, over the 24 same-axis pairs each: `key` frame 1.11% / focus 20.01% -> BITES; `gauge` frame 1.48% / focus 22.44% -> BITES. Widest pair on the sheet: gauge none <-> toll at 31.12%. Thinnest key pair: made <-> hue at gauge=none, 15.38%, which is thinnest because those two keys agree on which member is smallest (specimen 0 is both the first accessioned and the first hue past the cut), so the heap's apex does not move between them.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL SIXTEEN FRAMES, not from the default. Union 3.04 x 1.165 x 0.53 (x = across the four bays, y = the stack bay's column, z = apron back to apron front lip); diagonal sqrt(9.2416 + 1.357225 + 0.2809) = 3.29844, radius 1.64922. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera at 1.64922 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 10.2493 m and shows a 6.2670 m frame around a 3.04 m object — PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.58 the camera comes to 5.9446 m and the frame to 3.6349 m, which is 209.09 px per metre. Rasterised at that setting the subject's bounding box spans 75.7% of frame width and 42.9% of height, with 62 px of clear margin on the tight side (the right, which is the near side of an obliquely-viewed row and therefore the magnified one), and the subject covers 10.7% of the frame at the default tile and 11.0% at its fullest — far above the ~6% dilution floor and above the blank-render check. 0.55 was measured too (79.7% of width, 12.3% subject) and rejected: 43 px of margin on the near end is not enough slack for the showcase key light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model.

WHY THE UNION AND NOT THE DEFAULT: the box is identical at every value of `key` — the hall's footprint, plinths and apron are the same in all four — but `toll` adds two 0.470 m columns at the right-hand end of two rails, which widens the drawn content without changing the AABB (the apron already reaches x = 1.52). Framing off the default would still have been correct here, which is worth recording as the reason it was checked rather than assumed.

GAUGE CHECK AT 209.09 px/m, because foresight_range shipped a bench's 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a whole axis three pixels wide. Rank bar 0.038 m wide -> 7.9 px, and 0.034 to 0.272 m tall -> 7.1 to 56.9 px (a vertical projects at 0.9664 from this camera, so those are nearly true lengths). Toll column 0.110 x 0.440 -> 23.0 x 92.0 px. Mouth collar 0.124 to 0.258 m across -> 25.9 to 53.9 px wide; its top face, seen at 15 degrees down, shows 0.2092 of its depth, so it reads as a 5.4 to 11.3 px bright sliver rather than as its 2.5 px edge. Smallest specimen 0.076 x 0.045 m -> 15.9 x 9.4 px; largest 0.210 x 0.045 -> 43.9 px wide. Plinth 0.180 m tall -> 37.6 px. Ladder rung rise 0.072 -> 15.1 px. Nothing that carries meaning is under 5 px, and the critic's own downsample (crop ~585 px wide to 160, i.e. 3.7x) leaves the smallest meaningful mark, a rank-1 bar, at about 2 samples — which is the correct size for the smallest value of a gauge whose ceiling is fixed at 8.

THE ROW RUNS ALONG X AND NOT IN A 2x2, and that was a framing decision. A 2 x 2 of bays fills a square frame better and would have raised px/m by about 12%, but the camera pitches only 15 degrees down: a front bay 0.47 m tall hides the bottom 0.20 m of a bay 0.75 m behind it, and the stack bay is 0.955 m of column that would have blacked out whatever stood behind it. A row costs frame area and loses nothing to occlusion.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, checks the family list and builds the whole hall standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THE PILE IS A HASH, NOT A ROLL. The heap bay scatters its seven non-apex members from _index_hash(n) = fract(sin(n * 12.9898 + 78.233) * 43758.5453), the family's own hash taken character for character from combine_sphere.gd and math_objects_gallery.gd, keyed on the ACCESSION index and not on the rank — so the pile is the same pile every boot, every machine, at every value of both axes, and only the smallest member is lifted out of it to the mouth. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THE SORT IS DETERMINISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the one place this artifact could have leaked an ordering that differs between runs. Godot's Array.sort_custom is not stable, so _ranks() does not use it: it runs a hand-rolled selection sort over eight elements whose comparison is (value, index) and therefore TOTAL — no two members can compare equal, so there is nothing for stability to decide. The tied character (`sides`, three tied pairs) is resolved by accession index inside that comparison, visibly and on purpose.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_key / config_gauge metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks up to four ancestors for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against _is_key / _is_gauge, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value.

BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

THE TABLE BAY IS CONSTANT ACROSS `key`, BY CONSTRUCTION AND ON PURPOSE. At gauge=none it is pixel-identical in all four key tiles — verified in the replica: the leftmost changed column between any two keys is 278-282 and the table bay ends at column 236. One quarter of every key pair is therefore dead, and that is finding (1) in dna.note, not a fault. It stops being constant the moment the gauge is on, because the table's rank rail does read the key. If a future reader crops to the table bay alone and reports `key` INERT, they will have measured the argument and called it a bug.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `gauge`: the apron, the four plinths, all thirty-two bodies and the ladder's risers. Everything that changes between the four gauge tiles is measuring apparatus, which is that axis's whole subject.

TWO BAYS THAT SHOULD MEASURE THE SAME, AND IT IS NOT A FAULT: table and ladder have identical cost arrays (all zero) in every key, so they wear the same eight collars at `mouth` and neither grows a column at `toll`. They still LOOK completely different (a lattice against an ascending file) and their rank rails differ completely. This is finding (4) in dna.note. Do not "fix" it by inventing a sequential-access toll for the ladder.

TWO MORE THAT SHOULD MEASURE THE SAME: the ladder's rank rail and the heap's rank rail are the same eight bars in the same order in all sixteen tiles, because both claims yield ascending by rank. Finding (2). The stack's rail is that staircase reversed.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. There is not one Label3D, not one glyph, in any tile — see dna.declines for why, with the px arithmetic. No pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming its own variant. LabelFramer therefore has nothing to hang panels behind, and nothing enters or leaves the capture AABB on that account.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D (BoxMesh for the apron, plinths, risers, rail, collars and toll columns; a SurfaceTool prism for each specimen), there is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG and no particle system, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery default of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `gauge` is measured on [mouth, none] alone — which would return a LARGE number (predicted 27.74-28.15%) rather than a faint one, but it would be a verdict about two rungs published as a verdict about four.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 3.04 m hall is under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink. This artifact brings its own plinths; it does not want another.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? The four bays rank in screen X and the canonical camera sees the row at 35.5 degrees off its axis. A probe from directly above would separate the four arrangements even more strongly (a lattice, a diagonal file, a single disc, a scatter) and one from along the row would stack them into each other. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
